articles.title: Efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and stage 2-3 fibrosis: a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled study.
articles.abstract: Efinopegdutide is a pharmacologically distinct once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist with a relative receptor potency balance of approximately 2:1 under development for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of efinopegdutide in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH. We did a phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study conducted at 176 academic and community centres in 26 countries. We included adults (aged ≥18 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage 2 or stage 3 fibrosis. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1:1) to receive either efinopegdutide (4 mg, 7 mg, or 10 mg), placebo, or open-label semaglutide 2·4 mg, all administered subcutaneously once weekly. Randomisation was performed centrally. The primary endpoint was MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. The key secondary histological endpoint was fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis. Missing end-of-treatment biopsies were considered as failure for the primary analysis. This study is registered with EU CT, 2022-502647-35-00, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05877547, and is complete. Between June 23, 2023, and Dec 29, 2025, we screened 1704 participants. We randomly assigned 386 (23%) participants, of whom 381 (99%; 194 [51%] women and 187 [49%] men) received at least one dose of study intervention and were included in the analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar across groups; 239 (63%) of 381 participants had F2 fibrosis and 142 (37%) had F3 fibrosis; the mean age of participants was 53 years (SD 13). At week 52, MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis occurred in 31 (56%) of 55 participants in the 4 mg efinopegdutide group, 31 (63%) of 49 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 35 (61%) of 57 participants in the 10 mg efinopegdutide group versus seven (13%) of 53 participants in the placebo group (difference vs placebo 43·0 percentage points [95% CI 25·7 to 57·8; p<0·0001] for 4 mg, 49·5 percentage points [31·4 to 64·2; p<0·0001] for 7 mg, and 47·8 percentage points [30·7 to 62·0; p<0·0001] for 10 mg); 26 (53%) of 49 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. For the key secondary endpoint, fibrosis improvement of at least one stage without worsening of steatohepatitis occurred in 32 (43%) of 75 participants in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 39 (52%) of 75 participants in the 7 mg efinopegdutide group, and 26 (34%) of 77 participants in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group versus 16 (21%) of 77 participants receiving placebo (difference vs placebo 21·7 percentage points [7·1 to 35·7; p=0·0038] in the efinopegdutide 4 mg group, 30·4 percentage points [15·4 to 44·3; p<0·0001] in the efinopegdutide 7 mg group, and 13·0 percentage points [-1·2 to 26·8; p=0·072] in the efinopegdutide 10 mg group); 16 (25%) of 65 participants receiving semaglutide met this endpoint. The most frequently reported adverse events with efinopegdutide were gastrointestinal, with the highest rates among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg. Adverse events leading to discontinuation of study intervention occurred more frequently among participants receiving efinopegdutide 10 mg (nine [11%] of 79 participants) compared with the other doses of efinopegdutide (range 3-4%) or placebo (one [1%]). Treatment with efinopegdutide resulted in a significantly greater proportion of participants with MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis compared with placebo. The 7 mg dose showed the most favourable benefit-risk profile, improving fibrosis by at least one stage without worsening steatohepatitis in approximately half of participants after 1 year of treatment. These findings support the potential utility of efinopegdutide as a once-weekly GLP-1-glucagon receptor co-agonist in MASH. Merck Sharp & Dohme, a subsidiary of Merck & Co.

articles.title: Fecal Immunochemical Test Outreach for Colorectal Cancer Screening in Community Health Centers: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening is suboptimal among people in traditionally underserved populations, many of whom receive primary care at federally qualified health centers (FQHCs). Mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) outreach improves screening, especially in underserved populations, but questions remain about impact over time. To evaluate the effectiveness of centralized annual mailed FIT outreach delivered over 3 years to increase CRC screening in FQHCs. This cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted between June 1, 2021, and May 31, 2024. Sixteen clinics from 2 FQHCs in Southern California were randomly assigned to mailed FIT outreach or usual care for patients aged 50 to 75 years and not up to date with screening. Intervention components followed best practices for mailed FIT outreach and included educational primers, FIT kits, and telephone reminders. The primary outcome was the proportion of individuals up to date with any CRC screening after 3 years of intervention (point prevalence); screening at 2 years was a secondary outcome. Due to a resource constraint-related protocol modification, mailed FIT outreach began earlier in year 3, such that some individuals who completed screening in year 2 were not yet due for repeat FIT. Among 16 clinics serving 20 250 patients, 6 clinics serving 8334 individuals at baseline (4435 aged 55-64 years [53.2%]; 4896 female [58.7%]; 341 Asian [4.1%], 238 Black [2.9%], 2390 Hispanic [28.7%], and 4371 non-Hispanic White [52.4%]) were randomized to intervention and 10 clinics serving 11 916 individuals at baseline (6443 aged 55-64 years [54.1%]; 7250 female [60.8%]; 699 Asian [5.9%], 355 Black [3.0%], 4635 Hispanic [38.9%], and 4436 non-Hispanic White [37.2%]) were randomized to usual care. At year 3, screening was 39.4% (95% CI, 36.3% to 42.6%) in intervention clinics vs 36.5% (95% CI, 31.2% to 42.2%) in usual care clinics, which was not a statistically significant difference (2.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.2 to 9.0 percentage points). At year 2, screening was 37.8% (95% CI, 35.2% to 40.4%) in intervention clinics vs 27.0% (95% CI, 21.8% to 32.9%) in usual care clinics (difference, 10.8 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.9 to 16.7 percentage points). This study's findings suggest that centralized mailed FIT outreach could increase CRC screening in FQHCs serving populations with persistent disparities, although maintaining intervention fidelity and providing ongoing implementation support over time are needed for consistent impact. articles.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting  messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing. At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups. Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

articles.title: Digital and Coaching Interventions for Uptake of Cancer Genetic Testing: The MiGHT Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Germline genetic testing (GT) for hereditary cancer risk can inform cancer treatment, screening, and prevention, yet testing rates remain low. Alternative strategies are needed to improve facilitation of GT. To compare 2 patient-level interventions to increase uptake of hereditary cancer GT against usual care. The Michigan Genetic Hereditary Testing (MiGHT) randomized clinical trial analyzed self-reported GT outcome data from participants meeting clinical GT criteria between April 21, 2022, and November 21, 2025. Participants were adults (age ≥18 years) who met national criteria for genetic evaluation and had not previously completed germline GT recruited from oncology, primary care, and gastroenterology practices; research registries; and the general public in Michigan. Data were analyzed from April 30, 2025, to May 1, 2026. Participants were randomized to either telephone-based health coaching, a self-directed digital intervention, or usual care. Both interventions incorporated genetics education and motivational interviewing concepts. GT uptake was assessed at 6- and 12-month time points. The primary outcome was completion of GT by 6 months. The effects of study group on GT uptake were evaluated using logistic regression, adjusting for cancer history, age, gender, and race. A total of 793 participants (median [IQR] age, 64 [51-71] years; 458 [57.8%] female) were randomized to health coaching (261 participants), the digital intervention (265 participants), or usual care (267 participants). Overall, 31 participants (4.9%) reported completing GT by the 6-month time point, and 76 participants (9.6%) underwent GT across the 12-month study period. Compared with usual care, participants in the digital intervention group had higher odds of completing GT by 6 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 3.88; 97.5% CI, 1.27-14.80), while those in the health coaching group had higher odds of completing GT by 12 months (AOR, 2.25; 97.5% CI, 1.11-4.77). Participants in the digital intervention group were more likely to express intention to test at 6 months (AOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.44-3.93), whereas those in the health coaching group had higher intention at both 6 (AOR, 2.99; 95% CI, 1.83-4.95) and 12 (AOR, 2.29; 95% CI 1.29-4.15) months compared with usual care. In this randomized clinical trial of GT interventions, GT uptake was higher among participants who received the digital or health coaching interventions compared with usual care, although overall testing rates were low. These results underscore the importance of content delivery, motivational messaging, and alternative GT care models. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05162846.

articles.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone. This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete. Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths. The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications. articles.title: Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement. Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. articles.title: Remote multicomponent intervention for older adults with cognitive impairment in community settings: multisite randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment is common among community-dwelling older adults and represents a pragmatic target for community-level intervention. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a scalable, remotely delivered multicomponent intervention for older adults with cognitive impairment, integrated into community and primary care settings. This 6-month, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial was performed at two public health centres in South Korea, enrolling adults aged 60-80 years with cognitive impairment and preserved functional independence. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to a videoconference-based exercise and nutritional support programme or to usual health promotion services. The primary outcome was change in the Montreal Cognitive Assessment-Korean version (MoCA-K) score at 6 months; secondary outcomes included cognitive, functional, physical performance, frailty and depressive measures at 6 and 12 months. Among 140 participants (mean age 75.0 years; 60% female), equal numbers were randomised to intervention and control groups. At 6 months, the intervention group showed greater improvement in MoCA-K scores compared to the control group [2.3 points; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.4-3.1], and the difference was sustained at 12 months (1.1 points; 95% CI 0.3-2.0). The intervention was also associated with improvements in functional status and frailty at both time points. No intervention-related adverse events were reported. A remotely delivered multicomponent intervention improved cognition, functional independence and frailty in older adults with cognitive impairment identified through community-based screening. These findings support the effectiveness of scalable interventions integrated into community and primary care settings, particularly when access to in-person care is limited. articles.title: Concentrated Exposure Therapy vs Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Given the high prevalence, chronicity, and associated disability of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), optimizing treatment is a global priority. The Bergen 4-day treatment (B4DT), a concentrated exposure-based intervention, may reduce treatment burden and improve access to evidence-based care. Key exclusion criteria included schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, acute suicidality, substance dependence, and recent psychopharmacological changes. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 6 weeks, 8 weeks (posttreatment), and 3 months (follow-up) by masked evaluators. Patients were randomized to B4DT (including preparatory sessions) or an 8-week unguided iCBT program. The primary outcome was the change in OCD symptom severity, measured by the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS). Secondary outcomes included self-reported OCD (OCI-R), dysfunctional cognitions, quality of life, depressive symptoms, experiential avoidance, global functioning, self-esteem, and treatment satisfaction. A total of 253 individuals were screened, and 119 were enrolled after 53 were found to be ineligible and 81 declined to participate. Sixty of the 119 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 33.5 [10.1] years; 79 [66.4%] women) were assigned to B4DT and 59 to iCBT. Secondary outcomes consistently favored B4DT. Response and remission rates at 3-month follow-up were higher with B4DT (35 of 57 [61.4%] vs 11 of 44 [25.0%] and 24 of 57 [42.1%] vs 6 of 44 [13.6%], respectively). In this randomized clinical trial of 119 adults with OCD, B4DT was superior to iCBT in reducing OCD symptom severity, with sustained benefits. Its brief, concentrated format may represent a scalable strategy to improve access to effective OCD treatment globally. German Clinical Trials Register: DRKS00034236.

articles.title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed. To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%). The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized. Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250). The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications. The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups. Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. articles.title: Association Between Systemic Fluoroquinolones and Risk of Peripheral Neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Fluoroquinolone use has been associated with peripheral neuropathy in case reports, but there have been few noninterventional studies validating this association, and causality is unclear. The aim of this study was to estimate the association between systemic fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy relative to a comparator class of antibiotics, cephalosporins, using multiple databases to increase precision and assess the robustness of the results. Cohort studies were conducted using data from 2 databases of UK electronic primary care records, Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and GOLD, from April 1, 1997, to December 31, 2019. Among adults (age ≥18 years) without diabetes mellitus or previously recorded peripheral neuropathy prescribed systemic fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins, hazard ratios were estimated between fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy within 60 days of prescription using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighted Cox regression. Hazard ratios were similarly estimated for a positive control outcome of incident tendon rupture within 60 days of prescription. Risk differences for peripheral neuropathy were estimated using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator. Estimates were pooled across databases using fixed-effects meta-analysis. In total, 2,933,982 individuals prescribed fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins in Aurum (63.7% [n = 1,868,793] female; median age 49.5 years [interquartile range (IQR) 34.1-67.5]) and 995,457 in GOLD (63.5% [n = 632,033] female, median age 51.5 years [IQR 35.6-68.0]) were included. Of these individuals, at first treatment episode, 1,002,004 (34.2%) in Aurum and 381,734 (38.3%) in GOLD were prescribed fluoroquinolones. The estimated association between fluoroquinolones and peripheral neuropathy was close to the null at first treatment episode (pooled adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.77-1.20) and over all treatment episodes (pooled aHR 1.05, 95% CI 0.92-1.20). Hazard ratios were elevated for a positive control outcome of tendon rupture at first treatment episode (pooled aHR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53) and over all treatment episodes (1.76, 95% CI 1.52-2.04). Findings were not indicative of a substantive difference in risk of peripheral neuropathy between those prescribed fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins. Potential residual confounding is a study limitation. Study results provide some reassurance to clinicians regarding risk of peripheral neuropathy with fluoroquinolones relative to a comparator antibiotic.

articles.title: The effects of an integrated nutrition-sensitive WASH, gender and poultry-value chain intervention on enteropathogen carriage in Burkinabe children: A secondary outcome analysis of the SELEVER cluster-randomized trial.
articles.abstract: We examined effects of a 3-year poultry- and livestock-focused Water, Sanitation and Hygiene intervention (WASH) on enteropathogen prevalence and density (SELEVER trial; ISRCTN16686478). Clusters of peri-urban and rural Burkinabe households were randomly assigned to: Control (no intervention), SELEVER (poultry rearing, nutrition, basic hygiene practices, and women empowerment) and SELEVER+WASH (additional intensive poultry- and livestock-focused community-led total sanitation). Base- and endline fecal samples were collected from children aged 24-59 months and analyzed using real-time qPCR to detect and quantify 24 enteropathogen targets. Analysis of effects on enteropathogen carriage and density was by intent to treat using logistic, log-linear and two-part regression. We enrolled 1,054 children and analyzed 883 children with endline fecal samples (attrition 15.0%). Almost all children (94.6%) were infected with at least one pathogen. Children in SELEVER+WASH arm had lower prevalence of Shigella/EIEC infection and unconditional mean DNA content compared to control (prevalence difference: -9.0%, 95% CI: -15.4%, -2.6%; unconditional DNA content: -56.5%, 95% CI: -78.8%, -11.1%) and SELEVER arms (prevalence difference: -7.7%, 95% CI: -14.2%, -1.3%; unconditional DNA content: -67.5%, 95% CI: -86.0%, -24.2%). Prevalence and unconditional DNA density of Hymenolepis nana was also lower in the SELEVER+WASH arm compared to control (prevalence difference: -4.9%, 95% CI: -9.4%, -0.5%; unconditional mean DNA content: -52.4%, 95% CI: -77.0%, -1.4%) and SELEVER (prevalence difference: -5.2%, 95% CI: -9.8%, -0.6%; unconditional mean DNA content: -52.7%, 95% CI: -79.0%, -0.7%). A poultry- and livestock-focused WASH intervention was associated with reductions in prevalence and density of Shigella/EIEC and Hymenolepis nana infections in young children in Burkina Faso.

articles.title: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. articles.title: AGA/AASLD Clinical Practice Guideline on Management of Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
articles.abstract: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease associated with progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, liver transplantation, and premature mortality. Despite effective therapies, important challenges remain in the diagnosis and management of PBC, including identification of antimitochondrial antibody-negative disease, assessment of response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), risk stratification, treatment of patients with inadequate response, management of cholestatic pruritus, and prevention of recurrent disease after liver transplantation. The aim of this guideline was to develop evidence-based recommendations addressing these key areas of clinical care. The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) convened a multidisciplinary panel to develop clinical practice recommendations for adults with PBC. Systematic reviews were performed for 6 prioritized clinical questions. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework was used to prioritize clinical outcomes and assess evidence, and its Evidence to Decision Framework was used to develop recommendations. The guideline panel agreed on 6 recommendations. These recommendations address the use of PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies in antimitochondrial antibody-negative suspected PBC, UDCA as first-line therapy, liver stiffness measurement for prognostication, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA, linerixibat for moderate to severe pruritus, and UDCA prophylaxis post-transplantation to reduce disease recurrence. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low. The guideline emphasizes early diagnosis, optimization of first-line therapy, risk-based treatment escalation, symptom management, and prevention of post-transplantation disease recurrence to improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).
articles.abstract: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies. Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted. The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies. 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24). Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice. www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl; NL-OMON25059 (prospective registration; 4 Dec 2019).

articles.title: Efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of a nine-valent vaccine (ExPEC9V) for the prevention of invasive Escherichia coli disease in older adults: a phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trial (E.mbrace).
articles.abstract: Invasive Escherichia coli disease (IED) caused by extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) can lead to bacteraemia and sepsis. ExPEC9V is a conjugate vaccine targeting nine E coli O-serotypes that account for most E coli bloodstream infections. We aimed to evaluate ExPEC9V for safety, immunogenicity, and prevention of IED caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in adults aged 60 years and older. In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study conducted at 332 clinical sites in 20 countries (E.mbrace), we enrolled participants aged 60 years and older in stable health and with a history of urinary tract infection (UTI) within the previous 2 years. Participants were randomly assigned (in blocks of no set size with the use of interactive web response system, stratified by age and presence or absence of risk factors for complicated UTI) 1:1 to receive a single dose of intramuscular ExPEC9V or placebo. Participants, study-site personnel, and investigators remained masked to group allocation throughout the study. The primary endpoint was first IED in blood or sterile sites caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in the per-protocol efficacy analysis set (all randomly assigned, vaccinated participants without major protocol deviations); secondary endpoints included immunogenicity assessment in a subset of participants. Safety endpoints included solicited (safety subset), unsolicited (full analysis set), and serious (full analysis set) adverse events. A prespecified futility analysis conducted when at least 40% of the expected 53 IED events had occurred indicated lack of efficacy, leading to early study termination. We present final study results (data up to the date of the futility announcement), when 17 701 of the planned 19 800 participants had been vaccinated. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04899336). Participants were enrolled between June 30, 2021, and Feb 13, 2025. Of 18 844 individuals assessed for eligibility, 17 701 were enrolled, randomly assigned, and vaccinated (8858 with ExPEC9V and 8843 with placebo). The per-protocol efficacy included 17 637 participants (8822 for ExPEC9V and 8815 for placebo). There were 24 IED cases (11 in vaccine and 13 in placebo groups) caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in blood or sterile sites, yielding a vaccine efficacy of 14·63% (95% CI -106·57 to 65·38), indicating no protective effect. ExPEC9V had an acceptable safety profile, with more frequent low-grade adverse events in the ExPEC9V versus placebo group, balanced serious adverse event distribution among both groups, and no vaccine-related deaths. In this large phase 3 trial of older adults, ExPEC9V did not demonstrate efficacy in preventing first IED caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes, despite generating robust and sustained antibody responses. Development of the ExPEC9V vaccine has been discontinued. Johnson & Johnson and Sanofi.

articles.title: Non-antibiotic interventions to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in women: overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTIs), that is, ≥2 urinary tract infections (UTIs) in the past 6 months or ≥3 in the past 12 months, are common, have a substantial impact on quality of life, and cause major antibiotic use. To identify non-antibiotic interventions for prevention of rUTIs that have been assessed in systematic reviews, exploring their effectiveness, acceptability, and adherence. An overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on non-pharmaceutical and pharmaceutical (non-antibiotic) interventions for preventing rUTIs in women. Medline, Embase, CINAHL, Google Scholar, and Cochrane from January 2014 to May 2025 were searched for systematic reviews of RCTs assessing the effectiveness of community-based non-antibiotic interventions for preventing UTI in women aged ≥16 years with rUTIs. Studies in intensive care units, relating to people with indwelling catheters, or comparing different oral antibiotic regimens were excluded. There were no limitations regarding outcome measures or language. In total, 27 systematic reviews met inclusion criteria evaluating probiotics ( = 9), D-mannose ( = 7), vaginal oestrogen ( = 7), cranberry ( = 6), methenamine hippurate ( = 3), herbal medicine ( = 3), increased fluid intake ( = 2), systemic oestrogen ( = 4), acupuncture ( = 2), and vaccines ( = 2). Eight examined combination strategies. Cranberry and methenamine hippurate use are supported by systematic reviews, as is vaginal oestrogen among postmenopausal women, although questions remain around dose, duration, and treatment adherence. Reviews of probiotics, D-mannose, herbal medicine, acupuncture, and vaccines concluded that stronger evidence is needed. Increased fluid intake benefits women with low intake, but further research is needed on optimal intake. There was little information on treatment adherence or acceptability for many interventions. For effective interventions, questions remain about promoting adherence (vaginal oestrogen), or optimal preparation (cranberry), or duration (methenamine). For other interventions a stronger evidence base is needed.

articles.title: Antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with atrial fibrillation: an individual patient data network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Randomized trials demonstrated that in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and a P2Y12 inhibitor reduce bleeding compared with vitamin K antagonist (VKA) plus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with no increase in ischemic risk; however, important gaps in knowledge remain, limiting certainty and generalizability of these findings. In this patient-level meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluating antithrombotic strategies in patients with AF undergoing PCI, Cox proportional hazard models, stratified by trial, were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (HR, 95%CI). The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke, and TIMI major bleeding, respectively. The study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251130025). Six trials (10,634 patients) comparing DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor (4,083), VKA plus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT, 1,247), VKA plus DAPT (3,715), and DOAC plus DAPT (1,589) were included. The transition from DAPT to SAPT was recommended at 1 (1-3) and 3 (1-7) days in the DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor and VKA plus SAPT groups, respectively. At 1 year, the risk of the primary efficacy outcome did not differ across the antithrombotic strategies (reference group: VKA plus DAPT; DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor: HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.97-1.41; VKA plus SAPT: 1.14, 0.85-1.54, DOAC plus DAPT: 0.99, 0.75-1.30), without any statistically significant interaction between treatment effects and all prespecified subgroups, including age, sex, bleeding risk, and thrombotic risk. However, 14-day landmark analysis showed an increased risk of myocardial infarction and definite/probable stent thrombosis in patients receiving DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor or VKA plus SAPT in the early phase after PCI. DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor reduced the risk of the primary safety outcome compared with VKA plus DAPT (0.48, 0.38- 0.65) and VKA plus SAPT (0.62, 0.40-0.97); only a borderline reduction was observed compared to DOAC plus DAPT (0.66, 0.44-1.01). DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor reduced intracranial hemorrhage compared with VKA plus DAPT (0.21, 0.07-0.64). In patients with AF undergoing PCI, the risk of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke did not significantly differ according to whether patients received a DOAC or VKA, whereas a modest increase in risk with single compared with dual antiplatelet therapy cannot be excluded, given the higher risk of early coronary events. DOACs compared with VKAs reduced the risk of bleeding across all severity grades, including intracranial hemorrhage, whereas omission of a second antiplatelet agent reduced the risk of TIMI major or minor bleeding.

articles.abstract: Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) and 5-HT2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation. To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression. Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025. After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support. The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing. Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. From baseline to day 29, treatment with 12-mg intranasal mebufotenin benzoate vs the 0.3-mg dose (the primary end point) was associated with significantly reduced MADRS scores (mean score change, -11.1 [SD, 11.6] vs -5.5 [SD, 9.9], respectively; mean difference, -5.3 [95% CI, -8.9 to -1.8]; P = .003). The 8-mg dose also led to reduced scores from baseline to day 29 (mean score change, -12.5 [SD, 12.7]) vs the 0.3-mg dose (mean difference, -6.2 [95% CI, -10.2 to -2.1]; P = .003). MADRS reductions with the 8-mg and 12-mg doses were similar and significantly greater at all other time points from 2 to 57 days post dose vs the 0.3-mg dose. Day 29 response rates were 35%, 34%, and 12% and remission rates were 26%, 18%, and 8% in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively. articles.title: Predictors of Type 2 Diabetes Remission and Relapse After Metabolic-Bariatric Surgery or Medical-Lifestyle Therapy in the ARMMS-T2D Study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS) is effective in promoting remission of type 2 diabetes, but this outcome is not universally achieved. We identified baseline patient characteristics that predict diabetes remission and subsequent relapse after various MBS procedures versus intensive medical-lifestyle intervention. Alliance of Randomized Trials of Medicine vs. Metabolic Surgery in Type 2 Diabetes (ARMMS-T2D) is a 14-year, multicenter study of health outcomes in 262 patients with type 2 diabetes (68% women, age 49.9 ± 8.3 years, BMI 36.4 ± 3.5 kg/m2, HbA1c 8.5 ± 1.5%) previously randomized to MBS (n = 166) or medical-lifestyle management (n = 96). Predictors of remission (defined as HbA1c <6.5% on no glucose-lowering medications) and relapse were determined using univariate time-to-event analyses of prespecified candidate predictors plus agnostic, multivariate least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. Throughout a median of 11 years (maximum 14 years) of follow-up, 58% of participants randomized to MBS achieved diabetes remission versus 3% with medical-lifestyle management. Predictors of diabetes remission in univariate analyses included shorter diabetes duration, no insulin use, fewer glucose-lowering medication classes used, greater body weight, higher fasting C-peptide and insulin levels, and weight loss at 1 year (all P < 0.05). Diabetes remission predictors in multivariate analyses included baseline diabetes duration, insulin use, and weight change at 1 year (all P < 0.01). Diabetes relapse after initial remission in the MBS group was predicted by longer baseline diabetes duration and greater number of glucose-lowering medication classes used. Baseline predictors of diabetes remission and subsequent relapse among participants randomized to one of three MBS procedures or a medical-lifestyle intervention should help inform personalized selection of diabetes treatment.

articles.title: Thrombolysis in the Delayed Treatment Window for Acute Ischemic Stroke: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke but has traditionally been limited to 4.5 hours after symptom onset. This time-based restriction may exclude patients with salvageable brain tissue, especially those with wake-up or unknown-onset strokes. Multimodal imaging allows for the identification of viable penumbra beyond traditional treatment windows. This study compiles randomized evidence evaluating intravenous thrombolysis in imaging-selected patients treated after 4.5 hours. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central were searched through February 2026 for randomized trials comparing intravenous thrombolysis (alteplase or tenecteplase) with best medical therapy in patients presenting beyond 4.5 hours or with wake-up/unknown-onset stroke selected by imaging. The primary outcome was excellent functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale score 0-1). Secondary outcomes included functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and 90-day mortality. Fourteen trials involving 4192 participants were analyzed. Intravenous thrombolysis improved excellent functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0-1; risk ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.16-1.29]) and functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2; risk ratio, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.06-1.18]). Both alteplase and tenecteplase contributed to these benefits. Thrombolysis increased the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (risk ratio, 2.58 [95% CI, 1.58-4.22]) but did not significantly affect 90-day mortality (risk ratio, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.97-1.35]). In patients selected using advanced imaging, intravenous thrombolysis performed after 4.5 hours improves functional outcomes without increasing mortality, supporting a tissue-based rather than strictly time-based approach to treating acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of CagriSema in Type 2 Diabetes: A Dose- and Comparator-Specific Systematic Review and Bayesian Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: CagriSema combines cagrilintide with semaglutide and may improve glycaemic control and body weight in Type 2 diabetes. We evaluated its dose- and comparator-specific efficacy and safety. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Analyses were stratified by CagriSema dose and comparator. For HbA1c and body weight, efficacy/trial-product estimands were aligned where sufficiently reported, with treatment-policy estimates examined in sensitivity analyses. Bayesian random-effects models generated posterior medians and 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Six trials representing 4554 potentially eligible participants with Type 2 diabetes were included. Compared with placebo, CagriSema 2.4 mg produced between-group differences of -1.87 percentage points in HbA1c (95% CrI, -2.08 to -1.62) and -12.69 percentage points in percentage body-weight change (95% CrI, -13.78 to -11.61). Versus semaglutide 2.4 mg, the additional HbA1c reduction was modest and uncertain (-0.21 percentage points; 95% CrI, -0.62 to 0.11), whereas additional body-weight reduction remained probable (-5.84 percentage points; 95% CrI, -10.08 to -2.15). Gastrointestinal adverse events and adverse-event-related discontinuation were increased versus placebo (RR, 2.27 [95% CrI, 1.81 - 3.00] and 3.16 [1.50 to 6.87], respectively), while estimates versus semaglutide were less precise. CagriSema provides substantial glycaemic and body-weight benefits versus placebo. Its incremental advantage over dose-matched semaglutide is more evident for body-weight reduction, while comparative gastrointestinal tolerability and discontinuation risk remain uncertain.

Safety of withdrawal of pharmacological treatment after recovery from HER2 therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: the HER-SAFE trial.
articles.abstract: Heart failure therapy (HFT) is routinely continued in breast cancer survivors after recovery from anti-HER2 cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), despite limited evidence. HER-SAFE is the first randomised trial to assess HFT withdrawal in this population. In this open-label, multicentre, randomised controlled trial, breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD (asymptomatic, left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≥50%, normalised biomarkers) were randomised to HFT withdrawal or continuation. Antecedent CTRCD was mild (relative global longitudinal strain [GLS] decline >15%, LVEF ≥50%), moderate (LVEF fall >10% to <50%), or severe (LVEF <40%). The primary endpoint was a moderate or severe CTRCD event over 12 months analysed by intention to treat; secondary endpoints included serial cardiac function, biomarkers, and quality of life. Between July 2023 and June 2025, 90 patients were randomised (all female; median age 50 years [IQR 43-59]; median 17.3 months [IQR 7.7-33.2] since CTRCD recovery; HFT predominantly renin-angiotensin system inhibitors [98%] and beta-blockers [88%]) - 46 randomised to HFT withdrawal (1 lost to follow-up) and 44 to continuation. The primary endpoint occurred in 1 of 45 with withdrawal (moderate asymptomatic CTRCD) versus 0 of 44 with continuation (between-group difference 2.2pp; 90% CI upper limit 9.4pp). No cardiovascular deaths, heart failure hospitalisations or symptomatic CTRCD occurred. Cardiac magnetic resonance-derived LVEF remained stable in both arms at 12 months (between-group difference -0.8% [-2.0 to +0.4], p=0.21). Among breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD, HFT withdrawal was not associated with symptomatic events or significant between-group difference in LVEF at 12-months.

articles.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy - Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis.
articles.abstract: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not. We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points. A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported. Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. articles.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.
articles.abstract: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain. We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days. A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group). In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
articles.abstract: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming. To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support. Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets. A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system. Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system. In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

structuredAbstract.text: Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets.

structuredAbstract.text: A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). articles.title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract: Despite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. We aimed to compare the invasive interval cancer rates in women screened with digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised two-dimensional (s2D) mammography with those screened with digital mammography. TOSYMA is a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial done at 17 screening sites across two federal states in Germany. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing. Between July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set. Invasive interval cancers were detected in 70 of 49 299 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (invasive interval rate 14·2 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 92 of 49 456 women in the digital mammography group (18·6 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·55-1·06]; p=0·11). TOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening. articles.title: Haemodiafiltration, haemofiltration and haemodialysis for adults with kidney failure.
articles.abstract: Convective extracorporeal dialysis modalities, haemofiltration (HF), haemodiafiltration (HDF), and acetate-free biofiltration (AFB), remove excess body fluid across the dialysis membrane through an interplay of positive and negative pressures and accumulated middle- and larger-sized solutes more efficiently than haemodialysis (HD). This increased removal of larger solutes, combined with the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid in convective dialysis, is hypothesised to reduce the frequency and severity of symptoms during HD and improve long-term clinical outcomes. This is an update of a review first published in 2006 and updated in 2015. To determine the benefits and harms of convective (HF, HDF, or AFB) versus diffusive (HD) dialysis modalities, or expanded HD (HDx), in preventing all-cause and cardiovascular death, cardiovascular morbidity, fatigue, and vascular access problems in adults with kidney failure. We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and two trial registers up to 3 April 2025. Additionally, handsearching of journals and conference abstract books was performed, and the references of the included studies were reviewed. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing convective therapy (HF, HDF, AFB) with another convective therapy or with diffusive therapy (HD or HDx) for treating adults with kidney failure. Critical and important outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular death, nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, problems with vascular access, hospitalisation, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Two authors independently assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool. We summarised treatment effects using the random-effects model and reported risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous data with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the confidence of the evidence using the GRADE approach. We identified 62 eligible studies (6897 participants). In total, 54 studies (6525 participants) compared HF, HDF or AFB with HD (both high-flux and low-flux); two studies (24 participants) compared AFB with HDF; three studies (62 participants) compared HDF with HF; and four studies (163 participants) compared HDx with HDF/HD. Convective dialysis, compared with diffusive therapy, likely reduces the risk of death (any cause) (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.96; I² = 0%; 15 studies, 5463 participantss; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness) and cardiovascular death (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92; I² = 0%; 9 studies, 4761 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Cardiovascular morbidity was likely not different between convective and diffusive dialysis (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.22; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 2074 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Little to no differences were found between convective and diffusive dialysis on fatigue (MD -0.95, 95% CI -2.50 to 0.60; 1 study, 543 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), problems with vascular access (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.50; 1 study, 124 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), hospitalisation (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.37; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 600 participants; low-certainty evidence due to indirectness and imprecision), or physical quality of life (MD 0.66, 95% CI -1.08 to 2.40; 1 study, 538 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision). Direct comparisons between different convective modalities were limited and underpowered to detect meaningful differences. Convective dialysis likely reduces all-cause and cardiovascular death. Effects on nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, vascular access failure, and hospitalisation are inconclusive. Future RCTs should prioritise methodological rigour and could focus on unresolved questions, including the impact of convective therapies on patient-centred outcomes such as symptom burden, HRQoL, functional status, and intradialytic tolerance, as well as investigating barriers to uptake, evaluating health system readiness, assessing cost-effectiveness, and identifying strategies to promote equitable access. articles.title: Half-dose rivaroxaban vs antiplatelet therapy for preventing silent cerebral embolism after left atrial appendage occlusion: the HALO-SCE trial.
articles.abstract: The optimal long-term antithrombotic strategy after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) remains undetermined. The present study aimed to investigate whether half-dose rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) could better reduce silent cerebral embolic lesions (SCEs) and preserve cognitive function compared to antiplatelet therapy after successful LAAO. In this investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial, patients with successful LAAO confirmed 45 days post-procedure were assigned 1:1 to half-dose rivaroxaban or antiplatelet therapy group. Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and cognitive assessments were repeated at 90, 180 and 365 days after LAAO. The primary outcome was the patient-level incidence of any newly detected SCE during follow-up. Secondary outcomes included cognitive trajectories, SCE burden, and a composite of all-cause mortality, clinical thromboembolic events and major bleeding. Between December 2022 and February 2025, 164 patients were randomized. The patient-level incidence of new SCEs was significantly lower in the half-dose rivaroxaban group than in the antiplatelet therapy group (10/82 [12.2%] vs. 26/82 [31.7%]; P = 0.005). At 365 days, model-derived between-group differences favored the half-dose rivaroxaban group for both Mini-Mental State Examination (2.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.11-4.01; P < 0.001) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (2.67; 95% CI 1.07-4.26; P = 0.001) scores. The composite clinical outcome occurred in 2.4% of the half-dose rivaroxaban group vs. 11.0% of the antiplatelet therapy group (P = 0.057). In patients eligible for oral anticoagulation after successful LAAO, rivaroxaban 10 mg daily significantly reduced SCEs and better maintained cognitive function compared with antiplatelet therapy, with numerically fewer composite clinical events.

articles.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
articles.abstract: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain. To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock. Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026. Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter. The primary outcome of 28-day mortality and the key secondary outcome of kidney replacement therapy-free days through day 28 were analyzed using multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models, accounting for trial site and baseline patient characteristics. There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%) treated with the higher-threshold strategy (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.06], P = .62; adjusted risk difference, -0.4 [95% CI, -2.7 to 1.3] percentage points). Patients in both strategies for vasopressin initiation had a median of 29 (IQR, -1 to 29) kidney replacement therapy-free days (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.91 to 1.14]). In this large, pragmatic clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of 2 hospital-level strategies for second-line vasopressor management in septic shock, a strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower dose of other vasopressors did not reduce 28-day mortality compared with a strategy recommending vasopressin initiation at a higher dose of other vasopressors. articles.title: VERIFY: A Phase III Trial of Rusfertide Versus Placebo in Phlebotomy-Dependent Patients With Polycythemia Vera Receiving Standard-of-Care Therapy.
articles.abstract: Polycythemia vera (PV) is a myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by erythrocytosis. Rusfertide is a subcutaneous, injectable, hepcidin mimetic peptide that suppresses erythrocytosis. The phase III VERIFY trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of rusfertide in phlebotomy-dependent patients with PV and poorly controlled hematocrit. In VERIFY Part 1a (32 weeks), patients requiring frequent phlebotomy were randomly assigned (1:1, double-blind) to receive rusfertide or placebo with or without cytoreductive therapy. The primary efficacy end point was clinical response (absence of phlebotomy eligibility; weeks 20-32). Key secondary end points (baseline to week 32) included mean number of phlebotomies, proportion of patients who maintained hematocrit <45%, and mean change from baseline in patient-reported outcomes (Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System [PROMIS] Fatigue Short Form 8a [SF-8a] T score and Myelofibrosis Symptom Assessment Form [MFSAF] Total Symptom Score-7 items [TSS7]). Patients (N = 293) were randomly assigned to rusfertide (n = 147) or placebo (n = 146). Significantly more patients (n = 113, 77%) achieved a clinical response with rusfertide versus placebo (n = 48; 33%;  < .0001). Compared with placebo, rusfertide reduced mean ± standard deviation number of phlebotomies (0.5 ± 1.2  1.8 ± 1.5;  < .0001) and was superior in maintaining hematocrit <45% (n = 92 [63%]  n = 21 [14%];  < .0001). Rusfertide led to a significant improvement in the PROMIS Fatigue SF-8a T-score and MFSAF TSS7 versus placebo ( = .0252 and .0240, respectively). Injection site reactions, anemia, and fatigue were the most common adverse events. No deaths were reported. Rusfertide significantly improved hematocrit control, reduced the need for phlebotomy, and improved patient-reported symptoms versus placebo in phlebotomy-dependent patients with PV who were also receiving standard-of-care therapy.

articles.abstract: Early intensive blood pressure (BP) lowering is now recognized as an effective approach to improve outcome after acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). articles.title: Clinical Practice Guideline for Systemic Antibacterial and Antifungal Prophylaxis in Pediatric Patients With Cancer and Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients: 2026 Update.
articles.abstract: To provide updated Pediatric Oncology Group of Ontario clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with cancer and hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) recipients. In this update, we harmonized procedures and recommendations across both the antibacterial and antifungal CPGs. Systematic reviews of randomized clinical trials evaluating systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric and adult patients with cancer and HCT recipients were updated. Using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, an international multidisciplinary panel revised or formulated recommendations and classified evidence quality. Good practice statements were also created. The updated search identified 13 new randomized trials published since 2019 (eight antibacterial and five antifungal), resulting in 195 total trials. The panel maintained a conditional recommendation to consider antibacterial prophylaxis in pediatric patients with AML and relapsed ALL and a strong recommendation to use levofloxacin when antibacterial prophylaxis is planned. A new conditional recommendation was introduced to consider using no antibacterial prophylaxis in patients unable to receive levofloxacin. Strong recommendations to use antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with AML and allogeneic HCT recipients and to use an echinocandin or a mold-active azole when antifungal prophylaxis is planned were maintained. Three new good practice statements were added, focusing on drug interactions, infection prevention practices, and monitoring infection epidemiology. This update consolidates and harmonizes CPGs for systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with cancer and HCT patients. Future research should refine prophylaxis indications for different patient subgroups.
